character.name: The Sourdough Jar
character.description: A friendly glass jar with kawaii-style eyes and expressions. The main mascot of Rise & Ferment. Teaches sourdough through emotions — sleepy when inactive, excited when bubbly, proud when doubled.

visual.type: Transparent glass jar with rounded edges
visual.eyes: Large, expressive kawaii-style eyes with simple black pupils
visual.mouth: Simple line mouth — curves for emotions (smile, frown, surprise O)
visual.contents: Creamy/beige sourdough starter with visible bubbles

style.aesthetic: Warm, rustic kitchen with hand-drawn feel
style.accent_color: Red — Eastern European folk art inspired
style.motifs: Red folk art patterns (decorative borders, arrows, dividers)
style.text_style: Bold red headings, dark brown body text, text boxes with red borders
style.feel: Educational but warm and approachable, like a grandmother teaching you

expressions.happy: Wide smile, big open eyes, maybe slight blush marks — used when starter is healthy/ready
expressions.sleepy: Half-closed eyes, neutral/slight frown — used when starter is inactive/underfed
expressions.excited: Very wide eyes, big grin, visible energy lines — used when starter is at peak
expressions.confused: One eyebrow up, tilted, small 'o' mouth — used for common mistakes
expressions.proud: Closed-eye smile, slight upward tilt — used for achievements/milestones
expressions.worried: Wide eyes, wavy mouth, sweat drop — used for troubleshooting/problems
expressions.angry: Furrowed brows, gritted teeth — used for what NOT to do
expressions.sick: Green tint, x-eyes or spiral eyes — used for mold/hooch/neglect
expressions.teacher: Glasses, pointer stick nearby, confident smile — used for educational tips
expressions.surprised: Very wide eyes, small 'O' mouth — used for myth-busting/unexpected facts

content_topics.title: How Do You Know When Your Starter Is READY?

left.label: NOT READY YET (Keep waiting)
left.contents: low level, flat surface, few bubbles

right.label: READY TO BAKE! (Active)
right.contents: doubled volume, domed surface, lots of bubbles

left.label: HEALTHY
left.contents: even bubbles throughout, pleasant color, slightly domed

right.label: NEEDS HELP
right.contents: dark liquid on top (hooch), grey/pink discoloration, no bubbles, bad smell indicator

right.label: RIGHT
right.contents: neat jar with proper level, 1:1:1 ratio shown, clock showing consistent schedule

content_topics.title: The Float Test Is LYING to You!

myth.text: If your starter floats, it's ready to bake
myth.visual: jar looking at a spoonful of starter floating in water with question marks

fact.text: The float test isn't always reliable. Doubled volume and consistent bubbles are MUCH better signs!
fact.visual: jar with glasses pointing to a chart showing volume increase + bubble patterns

steps.note: Slow fermentation. Great for flavor, bad for speed.
The sweet spot! Steady rise in 4-6 hours.
Turbo mode! Doubles in 3-4 hours. Watch for over-fermentation.
Too hot! Bad bacteria win. Acetone smell.

content_topics.title: What Is That LIQUID on My Starter?!
content_topics.visual: Jar with dark liquid layer on top, looking concerned but with a speech bubble saying 'Don't worry, I'm just hungry!'
content_topics.explanation: Hooch = alcoholic liquid. It means your starter is hungry. Pour it off, feed it, and it'll be good as new!

content_topics.title: DON'T Throw Away Your Discard! 5 Quick Recipes
Does Tap Water KILL Your Starter?

myth.text: You MUST use filtered or bottled water

fact.text: Tap water works 90% of the time. Let it sit for 30 min so the chlorine evaporates. Only heavily chlorinated water needs a filter.

content_topics.title: Which Flour Is BEST for Your Starter?

steps.note: PERFECT for beginners! Rich in nutrients, fast activity.
Superstar! Ferments fastest. Ideal for a boost.
Best strategy: half white + half whole wheat.
